pdf-to-jpg.formula:
pixel_width = pdf_width_pt × scale
pixel_height = pdf_height_pt × scale

A PDF point is 1/72 inch, so an A4 page is 595.28 × 841.89 pt. File size grows roughly with scale² — doubling the scale quadruples the pixel count.
howTo: Upload your PDF file (up to 50 MB).
Pick a render scale: 1x for speed, 2x for crisp detail, 2.5x for print.
Click render and wait while each page is drawn as an image.
Download individual pages, or click the ZIP button to get every page in one archive.
keyFacts: Each PDF page is rendered to a JPEG image entirely in your browser using the pdf.js rendering engine.
The scale setting multiplies the PDF's native 72-DPI coordinates: at 2x an A4 page becomes about 1191 × 1684 pixels.
JPEG quality is adjustable from 40% to 100%; higher values keep more detail at the cost of larger files.
Every page downloads separately with a clear page-numbered filename, or all pages together as a ZIP.
The pdf.js reader library is bundled with the site; your document is processed fully locally.
